summary: The hand-rolled indexOf scan faithfully reproduces the old regex's rule, including its backtracking reading of unterminated quote fragments, while eliminating the stack overflow on ~15M-character literals. I verified equivalence by exhaustive differential fuzzing against the old regex (all strings up to length 8 over ', space, letter, tab, newline, double-quote plus 800k random quote-dense strings up to length 200: zero mismatches), confirmed the old regex still throws RangeError on the 15M case while the new code answers in 14-62ms and stays linear on quote-dense and fragment inputs. All acceptance points are covered by passing tests and no callers or existing behavior regress.
